2–5 years of service — resigning pays 1/3 of the full reward.
5–10 years of service — resigning pays 2/3 of the full reward.
10+ years of service — resigning pays the full reward, same as termination.

Balance = leave accrued so far this year − leave already taken. Leave builds up gradually through the year rather than all at once, so \"accrued so far\" is normally lower than the full annual entitlement until the year is over.

Estimate only, based on Saudi Labor Law Article 109 (21 days/year for the first 5 years, 30 days/year after). Actual carry-over, encashment, and company-specific leave policies vary — confirm with your employer or HR before relying on this figure.

This isn\'t a document scanner — enter a few terms from your offer letter by hand, and it checks them against Saudi Labor Law norms and common red flags for expat hires. Nothing you enter here leaves your device.
Extension beyond 90 days was agreed in writing
Only matters if your probation is longer than 3 months

Enter your offer\'s terms above and tap Check Offer
Saudi Labor Law Article 53 caps probation at 90 days, extendable once to 180 days only by a separate written agreement. What you entered is longer than that.
Long probation without a written extension
Probation beyond 90 days is only valid with a distinct written agreement. Ask your employer to confirm this in writing, or expect the standard 90-day cap to apply.
GOSI registration (at minimum the occupational-hazards branch) is mandatory for private-sector employees, Saudi or expat. Ask for written confirmation before signing.
Without a signed, ideally Qiwa-authenticated contract, you have little to fall back on if the employer later disputes the agreed terms.
You\'re being asked to pay recruitment or visa fees
Recruitment, visa, and hiring costs are ordinarily the employer\'s responsibility, not the worker\'s. Confirm this is really expected of you.
You\'d owe substantially more notice than your employer would — worth negotiating a more even split before signing.
Basic salary is a small share of total pay
End-of-service and GOSI are commonly calculated on basic salary (plus housing), not gross pay. A low basic can shrink those benefits even if your take-home pay looks competitive.
Nothing in what you entered matches a known red flag. This is a screening tool, not a guarantee — still worth a careful read of the full contract.

This is an automated screening tool, not legal advice. It checks the terms you enter against a small set of well-documented Saudi Labor Law provisions and common risk patterns — it can\'t see your actual contract and may miss things. For anything that matters, confirm with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (Qiwa) or a licensed legal adviser.

Enter the monthly take-home pay you\'re aiming for — this works backward through the same GOSI and salary rules used elsewhere in the app to estimate the basic salary and package you\'d need to ask for.

25% housing / 10% transport (the defaults above) is a common private-sector allowance split in the Saudi job market, and applies the same way whether you selected Saudi or Non-Saudi above — it\'s a package-structuring convention, not a GOSI rule (GOSI is what the Saudi/Non-Saudi toggle actually changes here). Employers vary it — some offer housing directly instead of an allowance, or use a flat transport amount. Adjust these once you have an actual offer to match it, or leave the defaults for a general first estimate.
